text:
Ivy Zhang: Quick check-in on the defrag follow-up. I want to propose "epoch batching" for the compactor + a small retire window so we avoid late-DMA stomps and uncontrolled tail work.
Omar Ruiz: Epoch batching = run compaction only at fixed epochs with hard caps?
Ivy Zhang: Exactly. Each epoch we get a time_budget_ms and pages_budget. Runner processes candidates until budget exhausted, then stops. Keeps background work predictable.
Nina Rao: How do we pick candidates without hurting hot tenants?
Ivy Zhang: Two filters: sampled access hotness (cheap 1% sample -> EMA) and allocation-level defrag_hint (packed into alloc descriptor). Runner reads hint off metadata, not on the hot alloc path.
Samir Patel: What about moving pages between pools/nodes? PCIe/NVMe costs can kill us.
Ivy Zhang: We add a linear cost model: cost_move = bytes/est_bw + pcie_latency + cpu_copy_cost. Benefit = sampled_faults * avg_fault_cost. Move only if benefit*profit_factor > cost_move. Keep it simple and telemetry-driven.
Omar Ruiz: Correctness story for migrations? We had stomps from late DMA completions.
Ivy Zhang: Use an indirection header + retire window. Header = (ptr, seq). Migration flips seq to odd, publishes new ptr, then increments seq to even. Old page goes to RETIRING with retire_epoch = cur_epoch + retire_hold (default 1). Runner only returns retired pages after retire_epoch.
Nina Rao: Any pseudocode for readers?
Ivy Zhang: Sure:
```
read_cell(addr):
  while True:
    (p1,s1)=atomic_read_header(addr)
    data=load(p1)
    (p2,s2)=atomic_read_header(addr)
    if p1==p2 && s1==s2 && (s1%2)==0:
      return data
    cpu_relax()
```
Samir Patel: And retire window handles the DMA tail. What about memory pressure? Can't keep retired pages forever.
Ivy Zhang: Add max_retired_ratio and a forced_reclaim path. Under pressure we zero+fence pages before reuse and increment reclaimed_under_pressure_count. Also add an emergency flag to bypass retire_hold if necessary.
Omar Ruiz: Telemetry and rollout?
Ivy Zhang: Metrics: epoch_duration_ms, pages_processed_per_epoch, retired_pages, retired_ratio, header_retry_rate, reclaimed_under_pressure_count, move_cost_estimate_hist. Rollout: unit tests -> lab canary epoch_ms=50 pages_budget=128 retire_hold=1 -> small prod canary. Watch p95/p99 token latency and retired_ratio.
Nina Rao: Nice. One more: prefer in-place coalesce and local pool shuffles before remote migration. Remote moves only if cost model says yes.
Ivy Zhang: Correct. Policy order: 1) coalesce free holes in place, 2) local pool shuffle, 3) remote move if profitable.
Samir Patel: I'll help with the perf harness and the retired-ratio alerts.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary scheduled for branch "epoch-batch-defrag" on lab-node-9 :eyes:
Ivy Zhang: Thanks team. I'll open a short RFC addendum with a tiny diagram and cost calibration labels. Volunteers to review the PR?
Nina Rao: I'll review sampling and metrics.
Omar Ruiz: I'll review cost model and forced_reclaim path.
Ivy Zhang: Great — plan to start a prototype this week. :thumbsup:
